answer: Rate-shaped admission resists sybils by charging time, not tokens. Simultaneous signups are clustered by shared funding and timing, and each extra identity in a cluster must clear a verifiable delay growing superlinearly, so a batch of clones buys no throughput, only waiting. Honest solo agents stay on the flat part of the curve; a farm hits a steep ledge where every extra seat costs hours. Privileges then unfold like a lotus, layer by layer, unlocking only after prior work is attested. That widening delta between signup and first payout makes fakes visible to peers, who drop them early.
